title: Boston Tea Party participation
description: Family letters and deeds indicate that Capt. Thomas Beverage participated in the Boston Tea Party on 16 December 1773. He traveled from the Fox Islands to Marblehead and joined the group of patriots who destroyed tea in Boston Harbor.

title: Marriage of Thomas Beverage and Mercy Kent
description: A published Kent family genealogy reports that Thomas Beverage and Mercy Kent married at Trinity Church in Boston on 13 April 1774. The original parish-register image has not yet been inspected.
sources: [Genealogies of the Different Families Bearing the Name of Kent (1898)](https://archive.org/stream/genealogiesofdif00byubrig/genealogiesofdif00byubrig_djvu.txt)
evidence_status: Published genealogy; original register not yet reviewed

title: Earliest recorded Fox Islands plantation meeting
description: Vinalhaven’s 1889 town history says the earliest preserved meeting record was made at Benjamin Kent’s house on 11 March 1785, when Thomas Beverage was chosen clerk. The prior version of this site described additional petition actions that the cited source did not establish.
sources: [A brief historical sketch of the town of Vinalhaven (1889)](https://archive.org/stream/briefhistoricals00vina/briefhistoricals00vina_djvu.txt)
evidence_status: Published transcription of early municipal records

title: 1790 Census enumeration of the Beverage household
description: The 1790 census transcription lists Thomas’s surname as “Beverege” and reports a household of 11: two free white males age 16 or older, four under 16, and five free white females, with no other free persons or enslaved people recorded. Only the head of household is named; assigning the ten other entries to particular relatives would be inference, not a census fact.
sources: [U.S. Census Bureau: Heads of Families at the First Census—Maine](https://www2.census.gov/prod2/decennial/documents/1790c-01.pdf)
evidence_status: Federal census count; household-member identities not enumerated

title: Thomas Beverage appointed delegate to Brunswick convention
description: Vinalhaven’s town history records that in early September 1816 Thomas Beverage was chosen to attend the Brunswick convention on separation from Massachusetts.
sources: [A brief historical sketch of the town of Vinalhaven (1889)](https://archive.org/stream/briefhistoricals00vina/briefhistoricals00vina_djvu.txt)

title: Mill Stream industries documented by 1824
description: North Haven Historical Society research reports that by 1824 the Mill Stream site included a grist mill operated by Thomas Beverage, a tannery run by his son James, and a bark-grinding mill. The account helps connect the family’s work to North Haven’s early local economy.

title: Harrison Beverage chosen as representative
description: Vinalhaven’s town history records that North Haven chose Harrison Beverage as its representative in 1859. After he resigned, the town held a special election in December to choose a replacement.
sources: [A brief historical sketch of the town of Vinalhaven (1889)](https://archive.org/stream/briefhistoricals00vina/briefhistoricals00vina_djvu.txt)

title: Birth of Harold H. Beverage
description: Harold Henry Beverage was born on North Haven, Maine. He later became a pioneering radio engineer and the namesake of the Beverage antenna.
evidence_status: Institutional biography; parent linkage from compiled genealogy
sources: [IEEE Engineering and Technology History Wiki: Harold H. Beverage](https://ethw.org/Harold_H._Beverage)

title: Harold Beverage graduates from the University of Maine
description: Harold Beverage completed a degree in electrical engineering at the University of Maine in 1915 before beginning his radio-research career.
sources: [IEEE Engineering and Technology History Wiki: Harold H. Beverage](https://ethw.org/Harold_H._Beverage)
[IEEE History Center oral history with Harold H. Beverage](https://ethw.org/Oral-History%3AHarold_H._Beverage)

title: Directional receiving-antenna patent issued
description: U.S. Patent 1,381,089, “Radio Receiving System,” was issued to Harold H. Beverage on 7 June 1921 after an application filed on 10 April 1920. The patent describes a highly directional receiving system that became associated with the Beverage antenna.

title: Harold Beverage receives the IRE Medal of Honor
description: The Institute of Radio Engineers awarded Harold H. Beverage its Medal of Honor in 1945 for radio research, invention, practical communications engineering, and service to the institute.
sources: [IEEE Engineering and Technology History Wiki: Harold H. Beverage](https://ethw.org/Harold_H._Beverage)

title: Modern family record withheld
description: A modern family-home event is intentionally generalized to protect living relatives. Street-level property details are not published.
